summary: Barbara Gerke is a Tibetologist who earned her D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under Charles Ramble and Geoffrey Samuel. She held posts at Humboldt University of Berlin (2011–2015), Oxford (attested 2017), and the Centre for the Study of Developing Societies.

Barbara Mittler is a sinologist and historian. She studied at Pearson College London, Mandarin Training Center, University of Oxford, and Heidelberg University, where she also held an academic post in 1993.

Tibetologist and religious studies scholar Barbara Nimri Aziz earned a B.A. from Queen's University at Kingston and a Ph.D. in social anthropology under Christoph von Fürer-Haimendorf at SOAS. She held a post at the University of Oran 1 in 2007.

Indologist Barbara Stoler Miller studied at Barnard College, Columbia, and the University of Pennsylvania under W. Norman Brown, Royal W. Weiler, and Stella Kramrisch. She was a professor at Columbia (~1968–1993) and Barnard, where she held an endowed chair.

Barbra R. Clayton works in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at McGill University under Richard P. Hayes and Katherine K. Young, also studying under G. Raj, and held an attested post at Mount Allison University in 2013.

Barend Faddegon was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at the University of Amsterdam from around 1898 to 1906. He served on the faculty at the University of Amsterdam from 1907 to 1944, becoming Emeritus Professor.

Barend J. ter Haar is a scholar of sinology, history, and religious studies. He studied at Leiden University under Erik Zürcher and Susan Naquin, later holding posts at KNAW (~1990–1994), Heidelberg University (~1994–2000), and Leiden (~2000–2013).

Barend Jan Terwiel studied at Utrecht University and the Australian National University. He held academic posts at ANU, UCLouvain, University of Munich, Leiden University, and served as Chair of Languages and Cultures of Thailand and Laos at the University of Hamburg (1992–2007).
Barnabé Brisson studied at the College of Juilly, École polytechnique, and École des Ponts ParisTech. He later held an academic post at École des Ponts ParisTech from 1820 to 1824.

Barry Kerzin, a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar, studied at UC Berkeley, USC, and under Geshe Namgyal Wangchen. He held posts at the University of Washington, CIHTS, and The University of Hong Kong (2014–2015, 2021–2022).
Bart Dessein is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who studied under Charles Willemen. He held a post as Associate Professor at Ghent University, attested from 2014 to 2019.
Barthold Georg Niebuhr was a historian who studied at Kiel University from 1794 to 1796. He held academic chairs at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1810–1813) and the University of Bonn (~1823–1831).

Basil Lanneau Gildersleeve studied at Princeton, Bonn, and Göttingen under Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl and Friedrich Wilhelm Schneidewin. A linguist, he served as Professor of Greek at the University of Virginia (1856–1876) and Professor at Johns Hopkins University (1876–1915).

Beata Grant is a scholar of sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She completed her Ph.D. at Stanford University (~1981–1987), held a postdoctoral fellowship at UC Berkeley (~1988–1989), and joined Washington University in St. Louis in 1989.

Beatrice Erskine Lane studied at Radcliffe College under William James, Josiah Royce, George Santayana, and George Herbert Palmer, and earned an M.A. at Columbia University. A Buddhist and religious studies scholar, she was appointed professor at Otani University in 1921.

Beatrix Pfleiderer, an Indologist, studied at the University of Maryland and Heidelberg University. She held academic posts at Maryland (1971–1975), Heidelberg (1973–1976), Hamburg (from 1982), the University of Hawaiʻi (1989–1991), and European University Viadrina (~1993–1996).

Bedřich Hrozný was a linguist and historian who studied at the University of Vienna and Humboldt University of Berlin. He held posts at the University of Vienna (~1905–1919) and Charles University (~1919–1952).
Beiho Takashima was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at Toyo University from around 1896 to 1900, later holding an academic post there.
Bemé Shyi Drol studied under Shechen Gyaltsab and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.

Ben Jiao is a Tibetologist who earned his Ph.D. at Case Western Reserve University in 2001 under Melvyn C. Goldstein. As of 2008, he served as Deputy Director of the Contemporary Tibetan Research Institute at the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences.
